*Source: Gapminder, life expectancy at birth, version 15 (5 April 2026), regional averages weighted by population; gapminder.org, CC BY 4.0.*

A newborn in Asia could expect to live 46 years in 1950 and 75 years in 2019: a gain of 29 years, the most of any region. Africa gained 22 years, the Americas 17 and Europe, which started highest, 14. The world as a whole went from 52 to 74 years. The sharp dip in Asia around 1960 is the Great Chinese Famine of 1959–61.

Gapminder's regions are wide: its Asia includes Australia and the Pacific Islands, and its Europe all of Russia and Central Asia.
